chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'but do not give them a promise in secret unless you speak in a goodly manner and do not confirm the marriage tie until the writing is fulfilled'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The secret is that the man says, 'I promise you the house of so-and-so family', then he seeks from her that she does not precede him (in marriage) when her waiting period expires.' I said, 'So (what about) His Words: 'unless you speak in a goodly manner'?' (He said): 'It is seeking the Permissible without confirming the tie of marriage until the writing reaches its term'.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'secret promise' and 'goodly manner' in Quran 2:235 according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic distinction between a 'secret promise' (wa'id sirr), which implies a binding intent to marry, and 'goodly speech' (qawl ma'ruf), which is merely expressing interest without commitment. This hadith establishes that a man may propose during the waiting period (iddah) but must refrain from finalizing the contract (uzmat al-nikah) until the period expires, ensuring the woman's status is clear. This interpretation highlights the Shia emphasis on preventing ambiguity in marital negotiations while respecting the sanctity of the waiting period.
